title: Repentance and the Care of God
english: Regarding Psalm 39:10, 11a: A great assembly is being filled from many and perfect ones. In this, the righteousness established through the faith of Jesus is being preached. Proclaiming this unceasingly and continuously, he says: 'My lips I shall by no means restrain.' He himself says: 'I knew my righteousness, having accepted this and being at home in it.'

Regarding Psalm 39:11c: He speaks of a great gathering collected from all nations, in which he says he is proclaiming the lion of God and the truth with boldness, saying these things are not hidden. Perhaps he proclaims the lion by declaring the forgiveness of sins occurring according to the lion, and the truth by being set in opposition to the shadow.

Regarding Psalm 39:12, 13: While I am doing the things foretold, You, O Lord, do not let Your mercies be far from me; have mercy on those who benefit through me. For the greater part of salvation does not arise solely from the working of God's mercy, but also the truth, taking hold, preserves [one] lest they be caught in a deception or some other error. For lawlessnesses pursue the judgment of enemies against the one fleeing them; if they do not grasp [them], the visual power of the soul is hindered so as not to be able to see the one catching [them]. Perhaps the lawlessnesses are being pursued by the evil powers working them. And they have multiplied beyond the hairs of my head; that is, the evils surrounding us are multiplying unperceived. With these many things having happened, being deprived of thinking rightly, we have been left abandoned from the heart.

Regarding Psalm 39:15, 16: Since the psalm is single-personed and is said of Christ, it must be said that those who have only the body saying, 'You used the Body for me, what also the soul confesses to have sought,' are lost—those who wrongly think this, praying lest they also be ashamed and fall into error. Just as those hurrying toward virtue have a command not to turn to the rear (for this is destruction), so the...

As evils rush upon them, let them hasten to turn back to the things behind, setting aside the bad intention; for then they are able to be shamed even in the sense of perception. Let those saying to me 'Well indeed, well indeed' immediately bring upon themselves shame. He who accepts sinlessness desires that no one should come into sin. But if anyone should go astray, 'well indeed', how he is immediately shamed for the bad and arrogant things he is doing, saying 'Well indeed, well indeed' (Ps 39:17, 18a).

Those seeking the Lord have an end to the seeking, which is to find him; and upon having found him, they rejoice and are glad with rejoicings and gladness. For someone having sought and having found God, and desiring to magnify him, wants to love the salvation of God, either the salvation from him or the Savior himself. And he loves [him] through all things and not for a little while. Toward the possession of good things, having confessed himself to God as weak, poor, and needy, he entrusts the care concerning himself to God, casting his care upon the Lord as upon a guardian (Ps 40:2b).

An evil day is the day of judgment, in which the God who pitied may pity the one pitied, and he is saved from every punishment; and perhaps even the whole existing life is an evil day, in which the Lord himself saves from those standing around (Ps 40:2b, 3a). Let the evil day and the day of punishment be understood. But he says 'to live' [him] the true life in the land of the gentle (Ps 40:3b, 4).

And he who is prevented from being delivered into the hands of his enemies is such as these, namely the souls of the enemies. And he will add to the one who understands concerning the poor and the needy, and these things following: 'For the Lord will help him at his bed of pain, and will turn his whole bed in his sickness, delivering him from human sickness, also granting him the health of the soul, even if there should happen to him some sickness of the soul (of which many things happen, as the apostle teaches, saying: 'Because of this among you...')
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.
